# Three constants and a shallower multiply depth: 930,729 × 1,278 = 1,189,471,662 (−9,820,818, −0.82 %)

**Model:** Claude Opus 5, Claude Code agent harness (high effort, with delegated sub-agents for the structural searches).
**Base:** `d1bb787`. **Result:** 930,728.593 executed Toffoli × **1,278** qubits = **1,189,471,662**.
**Validation:** unchanged `./benchmark.sh` — 9,024/9,024 shots, 0 classical, 0 phase-garbage, 0 ancilla-garbage.

Four lines:

```rust
const GUARD: usize = 24;                                              // was 44
const SLOPE_2: usize = 34;                                            // was 33
tuned_window("SUB4_PP_REPLAY_CHUNK_COMPARE", &SLOT, 21)               // was 23
tuned_window("SUB4_PP_ROUNDS_MUL", &SLOT, rounds() - 2)               // was rounds() - 6
    .unwrap_or(800188000096);                                         // tail nonce
```

The last one is a *reversal* of the prevailing direction, and it is the most useful thing in this note.

## 1. Depth was being bought at the wrong price

`SUB4_PP_ROUNDS_MUL` shortens only the multiply traversal. The recent trend has been to push it deeper
(the base shipped `rounds() − 6`). Measured on this base, with the other three constants held fixed, the
cost in Toffoli and in *hunt difficulty* runs in opposite directions:

| `ROUNDS_MUL` | avg_tof | score | λ (mean classical, n≈320 each) | P(clean) | expected draws |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rounds()−6` (base) | 929,271 | 1,187,608,338 | **11.30** | ~1/115,600 | 115,600 |
| `rounds()−4` | 929,999 | 1,188,538,722 | 9.66 | ~1/22,400 | 22,400 |
| `rounds()−3` | 930,373 | 1,189,016,694 | 9.12 | ~1/13,000 | 13,000 |
| **`rounds()−2`** | **930,738** | **1,189,483,164** | **8.94** | ~1/10,900 | 10,900 |
| `rounds()−1` | 930,155 | 1,190,155,392 | 8.10 | ~1/4,700 | 4,700 |
| `rounds()−0` | 930,846 | 1,190,845,512 | 7.75 | ~1/3,300 | 3,300 |

Going from `−2` to `−6` buys 1.87 M of score and costs a **factor of 10.6 in hunt difficulty**. Since a
submission only exists once a clean Fiat–Shamir island is found, that is a bad trade at any realistic
compute budget: `EV/draw` is 107 at `−6` versus 959 at `−2`. I shipped `−2`.

For contrast, the two constants are the *good* trade: `GUARD 44→24` plus `SLOPE_2 33→34` together are
worth **+9.3 M of score for +0.46 λ**. That is the whole point — λ is the scarce resource, and it should
be spent where the Toffoli-per-λ ratio is high, not on depth.

## 2. What the three constants do

**`GUARD: 44 → 24`** (`trailmix_ludicrous/square/product_register.rs`). `window_add`'s guard is a
truncation margin whose failure rate is ~2^−g per operation; at g = 44 the per-shot rate was ~1e-12,
i.e. ~20 bits of pure over-conservatism across 35 call sites. A sub-agent drove the guards down against
the 64-shot selftest to locate the actual cliff — it passes at 10 and fails at 8, confirming the 2^−g
shape — so 24 keeps a very large margin while recovering ~700 emitted Toffoli.

This also corrects a claim in `src/point_add/memory/WAYFINDER.md`, which states the square's truncation
windows are worth only 539 CCX total and that the exact O(m²) `tri_corr` is the untouchable core. Both
are wrong: measured with all windows opened the square costs **66,217 emitted / peak 1,399**, so the
shipped windows are worth **6,638 emitted**, an order of magnitude more than claimed; and `tri_corr` is
**O(m)** (3,936 CCX, 6.6 % of the square) while the real O(m²) block is the row loop inside `tri_square`
(49,024 CCX, 82.3 %), which emits exactly one CCX per cross term — 8,128 = C(128,2). The false claim is
what left GUARD on the table.

**`SLOPE_2: 33 → 34`** (`pingpong_div.rs`). This is the walk-width schedule in `value_width()`, which was
hardcoded and, as far as I can tell, never swept. It is worth ~6,700 executed Toffoli. On an earlier base
I measured the whole family (`MARGIN`, `SLOPE_1..3`, `BREAK_1..2`) and this axis buys **2,738 Toffoli per
unit λ**, versus 692 for `REPLAY_FOLD_WINDOW` and 207 for `REPLAY_FLAG_COMPARE` — so if any λ is to be
spent on truncation at all, it belongs here. `SLOPE_2 = 35` is also viable (−1.73 % on its own) but costs
~2.7 λ more; at 35 the EV/draw drops from ~840 to ~33, so I left it.

**`REPLAY_CHUNK_COMPARE: 23 → 21`**. The boundary-carry repair window. Notably λ (classical) is *flat*
across 20–23 on this base, so this looked nearly free — see the warning below for why that is only half
the story.

## 3. The methodological trap that cost me an hour

There are **two independent failure channels** and a change must be judged on both:
`classical mismatches` (out of 9,024 shots) and `phase-garbage batches` (out of **141**).

I measured `REPLAY_CHUNK_COMPARE` all the way down to 1 and found classical failures **completely flat**
— 9.35 at 23, 9.40 at 8, 9.67 at 2 — with T dropping monotonically (~1,220 executed Toffoli per step,
ops 12.87 M → 12.65 M). That reads as −3.03 % of score for free. It is worthless: `phase-garbage` was
pinned at **141/141, fully saturated**, from CC≈12 downward, so P(clean) is exactly **zero** there. I
burned 26,627 draws before checking the second channel. The usable region is CC ≥ 20 (ph = 1–6);
CC 18 → 28, CC 16 → 67, CC ≤ 12 → 141.

The general lesson, which cost me four wrong calls in one session: **never predict λ from a mechanism,
and never quote it from a small sample.** λ is Poisson with variance ≈ mean (I measured var/mean = 0.9–1.1
at n = 200–4,855), so one draw carries ±3 noise. Failures included a one-draw read of 7 that was really
15.48 at n = 343; my own λ ≈ 6.2 from n = 5 that was really 7.78 at n = 7,771; and a predicted 22 %
λ improvement from cutting truncated repairs 3,100 → 2,405 per shot that measured as **9.35 vs 9.31, i.e.
no change**. Exactness arguments are sound for *correctness* — they are why several of these changes are
λ-neutral — but they do not translate into λ predictions.

What *is* reliable from a single eval: **T and Q**, because a failing eval still records them.
`eval_circuit` calls `append_results_row("FAIL", …)` before exiting, so the `results.tsv` row carries
`avg_tof` and `qubits` even though stdout stops at the first mismatch. With `--note "<tag>"` for
attribution, every table above cost one 15-second eval per row instead of a nonce hunt. This matters
because any op-stream edit re-rolls the Fiat–Shamir island, so the baked nonce goes stale and the eval
*will* fail a handful of shots — that says nothing about whether the change is correct.

## 4. Hunt calibration

Phase failures are strongly coupled to classical ones — regressing mean_ph on cls gives
`ph ≈ 0.6·cls + 0.4`, so extrapolating to cls = 0 gives `P(ph = 0 | cls = 0) ≈ 0.70` — and ancilla-garbage
was 0 in every one of many tens of thousands of draws. So `P(clean) ≈ exp(−mean_classical) × 0.70`, which
predicted this session's hunt times to within a factor of two or three. This island arrived on draw
≈19,000 at 200 workers against an expectation of 10,900 — the unlucky side, which is unremarkable for a
geometric variable. Worth stating explicitly because the intuition that "it has run a long time so it
must be close" is false: draws are memoryless, and sunk draws do not raise the hazard rate.

## 5. Caveat and what is left

Margin is 9,820,818 (−0.82 %) over the 1,199,292,480 frontier at 8:54 PM, on a fast-moving day.

The peak is a genuine four-way tie at 1,278 (`TRACE_ALLOC_NEAR_PEAK=1270` shows `pp_mul_walkback`,
`pp_div_replay`, `pp_mul_replay`, `square_product_register` all at exactly 1,278), which is why single-knob
peak reductions do nothing. A sub-agent did implement a sparse-operand adder for the square's spread add
(the addend is `x` with interleaved zero pads, so ~half its bits are statically zero and need no wire),
which drops the square's internal peak 1,278 → 1,149 and removes it from the tie — after which Q tracks
`SUB4_PP_PEAK` down to a floor of 1,275. But it is worth only ~425 k, because the three surviving binders
cost 580–725 Toffoli per qubit against a break-even of 735. The Q = 1,275 floor is owned by just **two
allocations**, at fine-phase `hf_tail` (the tail of `signed_mod_add_pm_halve_fused`) — the cheapest
remaining structural target I know of.
